name: Segmented button
statusNote: Compose ships SegmentedButton.kt unmodified for the Expressive pass; only its deprecation notice is new. Build it for back-compat/migration only, and point new UI at button-group's connected variant instead.
summary: A row of 2-5 mutually touching outlined buttons sharing one outline, acting as a single- or multi-select choice control. Deprecated in favor of the connected button group, which MDC-Android says has "mostly the same functionality but with an updated visual design"; implement this only to read or author legacy M3 UI.

inputs.name: selectionMode
inputs.description: Single wraps segments in a mutually-exclusive selection (SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow, role RadioButton per segment); multi allows independent toggles (MultiChoiceSegmentedButtonRow, no exclusivity enforced).

inputs.name: segments
inputs.description: Ordered row of 2-5 segments. Each has a required label, an optional icon, a selected/checked boolean, an onSelectedChange/onCheckedChange callback, and an enabled flag.

inputs.name: activeIcon
inputs.description: Icon shown on a segment while it is selected/checked; defaults to a checkmark. Ignored per-segment if that segment supplies its own icon slot.

inputs.name: inactiveIcon
inputs.description: Icon shown on a segment while it is not selected; when omitted (the default) unselected segments show no icon and only the active icon fades/scales in on selection.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The row of segments, drawn with one shared 1px outline running its full width; no per-segment borders.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Optional per-segment icon. Shown by default only on the active/checked segment(s); can be forced always-on via a custom inactive icon.

variants.description: The only style; there is no filled or elevated segmented button.

layout.text: Only the first and last segment get outer rounding (the row's base shape split into a start-shape and an end-shape); every middle segment is a plain rectangle.
Segments overlap by outline-width (negative spacing) so each shared edge draws once, at full width, instead of doubling two adjacent 1px borders.

Content padding is hardcoded to 12dp at the start and end; there is no leading-space/trailing-space token in comp.outlined-segmented-button to source it from. Vertical padding reuses the common button's content padding top/bottom.
The row's minimum height is container-height; each segment additionally takes the common button's minimum width and height.

Within a segment, the icon (if any) sits to the label's start, separated by a fixed icon-label spacing; when a segment has no icon slot filled, the label recenters into the space the icon would have used.

states.text: With no inactive icon supplied, the active icon (default: a checkmark) fades in and scales in from 0, anchored at its bottom-left corner, and is never explicitly animated out on deselect — it is simply replaced when the next state renders.
The active icon's fade-in uses a separate, slower effects spring than its scale-in.
When both an active and an inactive icon are supplied, the two cross-fade instead of the active icon fading/scaling in alone.

Selected-state icon and label colors resolve through selected-icon-color/selected-label-text-color (and their focused/hovered/pressed variants); unselected segments resolve through the matching unselected-* tokens.
A focused segment resolves its icon and label colors through the selected- or unselected-focus- tokens, matching whether it is currently selected.
A disabled segment uses its own disabled icon, label and outline color/opacity tokens regardless of selection.

behaviour.text: In single-select mode, selecting a segment calls onClick for that segment only; the row does not clear sibling selection itself — SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow only groups segments for correct focus/semantics, so the caller must set the other segments' selected state to false.
In multi-select mode, each segment's onCheckedChange fires independently with that segment's own new checked value; no exclusivity is applied.

Border color per segment is driven by active-border-color/inactive-border-color (and their disabled equivalents), resolved and animated implicitly through the same interaction-driven color state as the container and content colors — there is no separate hardcoded border-color animation.

keyboard: Tab moves into and out of the row as one stop in single-select mode (selectableGroup); each segment is its own Tab stop in multi-select mode.
Arrow keys move the selection between segments in single-select mode, per the WAI-ARIA radiogroup pattern.
Enter or Space toggles the focused segment in multi-select mode.
semantics: Single-select segments carry an explicit RadioButton role, set on the segment itself — not on the row, which carries no role of its own.
Multi-select segments set no explicit role in SegmentedButton.kt; they rely on the underlying toggleable modifier's checked-state semantics, which assistive tech generally renders as a checkbox.
Each segment should be announced with its position in the row (e.g. "1 of 3"); Compose relies on standard radio-group traversal for this rather than an explicit live region.

notes.text: Only the single-select SegmentedButton overload sets an explicit role (RadioButton, SegmentedButton.kt:239). The multi-select overload never sets role = Role.Checkbox; its checkbox-like announcement comes only from the underlying toggleable/Surface(checked=...) semantics, not a hardcoded role.

The 12dp hardcoded content padding and the single flat size (no XS-XL scale) are the two clearest signs this component predates Expressive's per-size token system; do not try to retrofit size variants onto it.
There is no leading-space/trailing-space token in comp.outlined-segmented-button for the segment's horizontal content padding; it is a hardcoded 12dp in Compose instead.

Compose enforces no group-level minimum touch target for segments beyond ButtonDefaults.MinWidth/MinHeight on each Surface; treat the 48dp minimum touch target as general M3 accessibility guidance to apply yourself, not a modifier already present in SegmentedButton.kt.

comp.segmented-menu is a separate, newer menu-style token group (its own item/segment/shape tokens for a pill-menu pattern); SegmentedButton.kt reads only comp.outlined-segmented-button and never references comp.segmented-menu, so it is excluded from this spec.
